messages:
infra-bot: ALERT — service: inference-runtime-queue is reporting repeated pod OOMs and GPU driver errors across eu-west-1 pool. 90% of new requests are failing with 137 / CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED. More: https://incidents.internal/2632109876 :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: seeing the same in Grafana. Latency spikes then 5xxs. Autoscaler started 12 scale-ups in 6m then evicted nodes. Possible feedback loop. Paging oncall.

marta: I'm on it. First step — can we identify which model/version triggered the surge? Logs show heavy large-context requests to 'v2-llama-prod' tail.

ryan: Confirmed. Kernel logs from one GPU node: `NVRM: Xid 13` then container OOM. Crashloop with repeated restart. I pulled one pod logs:
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] ERROR: cuda_launch (0x2)
tensorflow: failed to allocate 14.7GB for tensor; process killed
[2026-03-15T12:04:05Z] INFO: container restart count: 6
```

alex: Autoscaler config shows aggressive target utilization 60% with burst policy + immediate scale-up. That explains oscillation: many requests -> scale up -> new nodes come up but KV cache cold -> memory spike -> OOM -> pods crash -> autoscaler thinks capacity still insufficient -> more scale actions.

oncall-sre: we need immediate mitigation: 1) pause autoscaling 2) pin traffic to smaller model variant or cpu fallback 3) cordon flaky nodes 4) increase node cooldown. I'll take steps 1 and 3.

marta: I'll push a quick runtime change to limit max_batch_size and enable kv-prefix caching for the hot model. Patch:
```yaml
routes:
  - model: v2-llama-prod
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
    kv_cache_ttl: 60000
```
Applying now.

ryan: Pausing autoscaler by setting annotation `autoscaler.k8s.redwood/pause: true` on cluster eu-west-1. Command: `kubectl annotate cluster eu-west-1 autoscaler.k8s.redwood/pause=true --overwrite`. Doing it.

infra-bot: ACTION — autoscaler annotations updated by oncall-sre. Scale actions paused.

alex: Cordoned two nodes that had repeated Xid errors: gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-21. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` & `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-node-21` in progress.

sophie: Customer impact: We're seeing degraded throughput for customers in EU region; CS ticket #CS-8792 created. I'll post a short status update: "We are investigating increased errors in inference runtime affecting EU traffic — mitigation in progress."

ops-bot: STATUS — Deploy job 2389 (kv-cache patch) succeeded on router group eu-west-1. No rolling restarts required.

ryan: Even after cordon and autoscaler pause, one hot pod still spikes memory. I set a temporary limit on model concurrency to 1 for v2-llama-prod: `redwoodctl routes update v2-llama-prod --concurrency 1`. That should reduce peak memory per pod.

marta: Also toggled quantized fallback on the route: `model_variant: v2-llama-8bit` for new requests. This will lower GPU memory pressure but slightly affects latency/quality.

oncall-sre: Good. Observing 5xx rate dropping from 78% -> 24% over 6 minutes. Heap / GPU mem pressure trending down on most nodes.

infra-bot: ALERT — node gpu-node-13 experienced kernel page fault before; team recommends cordon for preventive.

alex: Cordoned gpu-node-13 as well. Evicted pods moved to CPU-backed nodes where available. Some customers will see slower responses but service stays up.

ryan: We're also increasing autoscaler cooldown to 10m to prevent repeated scale-ups once we unpause. Patch to HPA: `spec.behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600` applied.

marta: Added a temporary circuit-breaker on ingress that rejects requests with context length > 30k tokens with 413 to avoid large-batch jobs triggering another surge. Command: `redwoodctl ingress update --max-context-tokens 30000`.

sophie: CS update posted: "Mitigations deployed. We’re limiting very large requests and routing to quantized model to reduce GPU memory usage. Impact: increased latency for some EU customers; errors decreasing. Will follow up with timeline."

oncall-sre: Monitoring for 20m. If stable, we can unpause autoscaler with new cooldown and variant limits. Next steps if instability returns: enable soft-throttling per-project, shift burst capacity to reserved CPU pool, and open a pager to infra-ml for model memory regression.

ryan: Noted a strange pattern in kube events: `FailedCreate: pod triggered OOM but node still reports available mem`. Could be runaway allocator on GPU driver — opened a ticket to cloud provider support (CB-5541).

infra-bot: METRIC — error_rate: 5xx_eu = 12% (was 78%). GPU memory utilization eu-west-1 = 68% (was 92%).

oncall-sre: Okay plan: hold autoscaler paused, keep node cooldown 10m, keep concurrency limit and quantized variant, keep circuit-breaker. I'll hand off to next oncall in 40m if stable.

marta: I'm going to bake a safer autoscale profile for v2-llama-prod: higher target utilization (75%), longer scale-up window, and pre-warm step to start small GPU VMs with warm cache. Will submit PR once incident is stable.

alex: For immediate safety, I'll mark the problematic GPU driver image as quarantine: `node.k8s.redwood/quarantine=true` so new nodes from that image don't join autoscaling pool.

sophie: CS will send a customer advisory to affected accounts with explanation and ETA for a postmortem.

ops-bot: REMINDER — next oncall handoff at 2632111700 UTC.

oncall-sre: Handoff notes: paused autoscaler, cordoned nodes gpu-node-13/17/21, concurrency=1 for v2-llama-prod, model_variant=v2-llama-8bit for new requests, cooldown=600s, circuit-breaker max-context=30000. If errors go back above 25% reopen page to infra-ml.

customer-success: Thanks team — will keep customers informed and collect affected request IDs for later analysis.

oncall-sre: Closing live mitigation sequence. Will keep the thread open and update if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
